review.verdict: Casting is correct (human mathematician, two AI robots) and the paper-cutout style is consistent, but the right-panel robot and the human overlap into a confusing clipped blob straddling the divider, the calendar is too small to read, and a large empty green ground wastes composition—this doesn't clear the bar for publish-ready polish or clarity.
revisionNotes: bot-tip and math-human clip into each other near the divider, forming an unreadable merged blob—move bot-tip fully onto 'right-third' (drop the -40px offset) and give math-human more breathing room on the left so each panel reads separately.

The label 'Unnoticed for months' cuts across both figures' legs (lint flagged it was shoved -111px to fit); re-anchor it directly under tipbox with clear padding instead of overlapping neighboring components.

Calendar at scale 0.9 in the corner reads as a stray scribble, not a torn two-month calendar—scale to ~1.3, add clearer torn-edge silhouette and visible dust cross-hatching, and give it its own clear space away from the divider.
Bottom half of the frame is an empty green ground shape with no story content—raise the horizon or add a small prop (e.g., chalk dust pile, police tip-line sign) so the lower half isn't wasted.

Keep left-panel elements (blackboard, bot-proof, math-human) strictly left of the divider and right-panel elements (bot-tip, tipbox, calendar) strictly right—right now they straddle the line and defeat the two-panel structure.

Vertical-divider split-panel layout plus the teal/cream/orange palette closely echoes two recent sloppers (robots split by a line; 'Records' tug-of-war)—try a different panel treatment, like a diagonal split or a single unified scene, for more novelty.

review.verdict: Fails: the cast is correctly handled (humans human, AI robotic) and kindness is fine, but the planned two-panel split was dropped in favor of one crowded row of seven elements, the 'Unnoticed' label overlaps three other components, the blackboard reads as a few scattered dashes rather than a flood of proofs, and stray dust/sign props misread as golf balls and a tee.
revisionNotes: Composition: brief called for two panels split by a vertical divider; render merged everything into one crowded row of 7 elements (2 robots, human, blackboard, calendar, tipbox, dust, sign-post) — restore the divider, or cut 2-3 components to stay under the 3-4 element guideline.

Polish: the 'Unnoticed' label pill clips across the human's legs, the tipbox, and the right robot's leg — shrink it to scale 0.8 and anchor it directly under tipbox only, clear of the human and bot-tip.
Clarity: the blackboard's chalk marks are too sparse and uniform to read as 'a flood of new proofs' — densify the raw svg lines with more rows/varied lengths so the board looks genuinely overflowing.

Polish: the white circles at bot-proof's feet and the post+circle at bot-tip's feet read as golf balls and a golf tee, not chalk dust or a sign — redraw dust-pile as fine debris under the board, and rework tip-sign so it doesn't resemble sports props.
Coherence: pull tipbox and the folded note closer to bot-tip's lowered hand (currently floating mid-gap) so the 'slipping a note into the box' action is legible at a glance.
Novelty: the beige-sky/teal-ground palette and horizontal lineup near the horizon closely echo several recent pieces — try a different ground color or vertical staging to stand out.

review.verdict: A fair, kind two-panel gag with correct human/robot casting, but it leans on a split-divider layout already used in recent sloppers and a couple of props (abstract blackboard marks, unlabeled tip box, calendar X's) need clearer execution to sell the joke instantly.
revisionNotes: Novelty: a vertical-divider split-panel card with a robot on each side has appeared in at least two recent sloppers; vary the framing (diagonal split, single continuous scene, or offset panels) so this doesn't read as a repeat layout.

Clarity: the blackboard's equation marks read as plain tally dashes/barcode, not proofs; vary the raw shapes (fraction bars, sigma squiggles, small circles) and scale them up so 'flood of new proofs' is legible.
Clarity: the tip box has no cue it's a police tip line (reads as a donation/suggestion box); add a small badge or star prop on the box so the second robot's action is unambiguous.
Polish: the 'Unnoticed' label straddles the center divider; move its anchor further right (e.g. x=0.85) so it sits fully in the right panel.
Clarity: the torn calendar's two X marks read like a ghost's eyes rather than crossed-off months; swap for strike marks across a few curling torn pages to better sell two months passing.
